title: Parse raw prices with static and unbound references

blocks.text: A **static** method reference (`Integer::parseInt`, `Math::abs`, `Objects::nonNull`) passes the interface's arguments straight to a static method. An **unbound** one (`String::trim`, `String::isEmpty`) calls the method on the argument itself. Both look like `ClassName::method`; which one you have depends on how the method is declared.
Write two methods in `Prices` (the page writes them as pipelines of method references):

items: `List<Integer> parse(List<String> raw)` parses every usable entry, in order. `null` entries and entries that are empty once trimmed are skipped; spaces around a number are ignored.
`List<Integer> magnitudes(List<Integer> values)` returns each value's absolute value.

blocks.text: The order of the steps matters: think about what each reference needs to be true of its argument before it runs.

cases.says: It parses plain numbers in order and gives each value's magnitude.
A null entry is skipped with Objects::nonNull before any reference calls a method on it.
Spaces around a number are trimmed before Integer::parseInt sees it.
An entry of spaces only is skipped; it must be trimmed before the emptiness check.

concepts: Static and unbound references line up in one pipeline, and the order of the steps decides what each reference receives.
A static method reference passes the interface's arguments straight to the static method, with no receiver.
